summary: C-0005: However, sociocognitive factors (expectancy, context, demand) demonstrably modulate hypnotic responding, and induction effects are often small relative to non-hypnotic suggestibility — so social factors are real and significant contributors.
content: C-0005 (claim): Sociocognitive factors (response expectancy, context, demand characteristics, motivation) demonstrably modulate hypnotic responding and must be part of any complete account. Hypnotic and non-hypnotic suggestibility correlate strongly (r=0.67 behavioral, r=0.82 subjective). Inductions often have small or no incremental effect beyond suggestion alone (Zahedi 2024 review EV-0010). Spanos (EV-0018) shows involuntariness is partly shaped by self-presentation/demand. Kirsch response-set theory (EV-0008) shows the hypnotic context 'intensifies the effects of suggestion' via expectancy. supports: EV-0008, EV-0010, EV-0013, EV-0018. contradicts: (qualifies C-0004).
